title: Johannes Brahms's birth chart
metaDescription: Johannes Brahms's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 16.6° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.1° separates the Sun and Mars from an exact sextile; at that range identity and drive read as one mechanism. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 16.6° Taurus — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that Mercury, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Aries (22.1°), Venus in Gemini (1.8°), Mars in Cancer (16.7°): thought that arrives already in motion, attraction that begins as conversation, effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — the Sun sextile Mars, 0.1° of separation. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional. Behind it, Mercury sextile Uranus at 0.3°, and Mercury conjunction Jupiter at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, one placement stands out. Mars in Cancer at 16.7° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 earth, 3 fire, 2 air, 1 water by element and 5 cardinal, 2 fixed, 2 mutable by modality. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. Venus, Saturn and Neptune were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.6° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
